title: Keys
description: Generated by `cargo run -p tmark-ir --example schema` from the Rust types of tmark-ir; do not edit. The typed subset of the front matter (spec §Front matter). Serialises to the canonical layout: metadata at the root, the rest under `press`.

date.description: ISO date, free text, or `commit`; kept as written.

title.description: `None` when absent (the first heading is promoted), `Some(None)` for `title: null` (spec §Header: opt out of promotion).

counter.description: Counter prefix of a theorem-type admonition.

reference.description: Text of the "See page N" link, with a `{page}` field.

Author.description: Spec §Front matter: `authors: [{name, affiliation}]`. A bare string item (`authors: [Ada Lovelace]`) is the name alone (C9: TMark tolerates what TeXSmith accepts).

name.description: Label word, used in references and diagnostics.

ref.description: Template a reference renders, with `{name}` and `{number}` fields.

Declare.description: `declare`: what things *are*. Spec §Front matter, §Counters, §Admonition, §Glossary and acronyms.

acronyms.description: Structure owned by TeXSmith for now; kept as JSON.

glossary.description: Spec §Glossary and acronyms: both accepted spellings of the declaration land in the same struct.

Epigraph.description: Spec §BlockQuote: `epigraph: {quote, source}`, the document's epigraph as plain text. The key says what the epigraph is, never where it goes: no writer reads it, and a consumer that decides where an epigraph belongs splices a `> {.epigraph}` quote there itself.

GlossaryDecl.description:
The glossary declaration, `declare.glossary`. Spec §Glossary and acronyms: two spellings reach this one struct.

The *flat* spelling is a mapping of term to definition (`api: An interface`, or `api: {name, description}`); the *structured* one names its parts (`style`, `groups`, `entries`) and keeps the terms under `entries`. The two may be mixed: `style`, `groups` and `entries` are structural wherever they appear at the top level, every other key there is a term. A term of one of those three names is therefore only writable under `entries` — where it wins over a flat key of the same name. `glossary: long` (TeXSmith 0.6) names a style and no term.

`style` and `groups` are not terms and never reach the glossary registry: they are form, read from here by the consumer that renders the per-group tables (TeXSmith's `ts-glossary` fragment).

entries.description: The terms, whichever spelling declared them.

groups.description: Group key to its heading; a template prints one table per group.

GlossaryEntry.description: A glossary term. `api: An interface` sets `description`; the object form takes `name` (the short form), `description`, `long` and the `group` the entry belongs to.

group.description: Key of the `groups` entry this term is listed under.

long.description: The expanded form of an acronym, when it differs from the description.

GlossaryGroup.description: A glossary group: `core: Core terms` or `core: {title: Core terms}`.

Press.description: The `press` namespace, restricted to the keys TMark reads.

base_level.description: What a top-level `#` maps to (`chapter`, `section`, …). Spec §Header.

features.description: Spec §Feature registry: dotted name to switch.

Scope.description: Numbering scope of a counter. Spec §Counters (`scope`).

bibliography.description: A map of key to DOI URL or pybtex-shaped entry, or a list of `.bib` paths; kept as JSON, `tmark-registry` interprets it.
